Commentary.Commentary: The Australians have made a definite statement with this aggressive win. This series win has certainly helped ease the pain from their Test whitewash. It will be Sri Lanka nursing wounds this time, both figuratively and literally, as an injured Angelo Mathews will attest. They will be back without their captain for the final ODI of the series at Pallekele and will look to end it on a more positive note. Do join us as we cover all the action from that match at 1430 IST on the 4th of September. Until then, goodbye and take care!

Victorious Australian captain, David Warner says that he is very pleased and that it was a hard-fought effort. Adds that his team came out and bowled well. He feels the conditions were quite tough. Says that his side looks to entertain the crowd and they tried their best to do that. For him, it doesn't matter whether the track is very good or like this one, he and his side always try to start off positively. He feels it is not easy to climb out of a form slump but is in good spirits. He is very happy with the way George Bailey batted and played a variety of shots. Compliments him by calling him the backbone of the team and rock in the middle order.

Sri Lankan stand-in captain, Dinesh Chandimal says that he and his side are very disappointed with their performance. He feels they didn't click as a batting side and the way they played. Initially, they wanted to score 260-270 but failing that, the bowlers couldn't do much. (On Angelo Mathews' injury) The skipper says that Angelo has suffered a calf strain and will be missed. He looks forward to seeing him again against SA. Mathews has a scan tomorow. He thinks Sachith Pathirana bowled very well and slow, with him making the most of the opportunities presented. According to him, the no ball on which Head was bowled was a turning point in the game and that they we had  a great chance to end it. He ends by complementing the Australians on their batting and gives them credit for their performance.

Man of the Match, John Hastings says that there are days when a player plays well. He found the conditions to be hot, sticky and very uncomfortable but made the most of them and the winds. He feels that he got lucky today and while he has been absent from the ODI squad for a bit, is happy with what he has provided. He thinks he could have started better but found his rhythm. He considers this a huge win for himself and his side and says that it is always nice to win a series, especially in his country's colours.

After a quickfire start, the Australians stuttered a bit as Sachith Pathirana hunted down three wickets in a space of 5 balls and gave a real scare to the World Champions. However, as has been the case in the series, the Australian middle order rose to the occasion and avoided any more hiccups. However, Travis Head got a second life after getting bowled on a no ball. George Bailey joined forces with youngster Travis Head and threaded a winning century stand. The former Aussie captain remained unbeaten on 90 as Matthew Wade launched a biggie to finish the game in style.

Australia adopted some brilliant tactics to counterattack from the word go and Aaron Finch, in particular, batted like a train on fire. He notched up his fifty in just 18 balls (joint fastest for Australia), and provided a flying start to the Aussies. George Bailey suffered a score but got another life when his catch was dropped early on.

A convincing win for Australia as they take an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series. The blueprint for this ODI was also on similar lines. Sri Lanka lost early wickets and then a good partnership brought them back in the game. They somehow reached a total of around 210-220 and hoped that their spinners will do the job. However, it wasn't meant to be tonight.

SIX! AUSTRALIA CLINCH THE SERIES! Wade ends the match in style, striking that fuller ball cleanly over mid-wicket. He lifts his hands in celebration and doesn't bother to see where the ball lands. It lands in the stands for a maximum. He walks towards Bailey and envelopes him in a bear hug. After the hug, Bailey sneaks away and picks up a couple of wickets for himself. AUSTRALIA WIN BY 6 WICKETS AND 114 BALLS REMAINING!

21st ODI fifty for George Bailey!

Fifty for Bailey! A brilliant knock by the former Aussie skipper. He didn't let the scoring tempo go down from the time he came out to bat. Finch provided the start and he has just capitalized over it. Tossed up ball on off, GB drives it through mid off for a run. Australia will hope that he bats through!
Stretches forward to a full ball and defends it with the spin to covers.
Slow loopy ball on middle, bowled with a round-arm action, it's on middle and Bailey defends it off his front foot.
Gets back to a short ball and cuts it through point for a couple of runs.
Short on off, cut straight to point to end the over.
Spinning down the leg side, Bailey pulls it down to deep square leg for a single.
Lunges to a full ball in defense but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.
50-run stand between Head and Bailey.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Loopy ball on off, reverse swept through covers for a single.

OUT! LBW! Pathirana strikes again. Flighted around off, the ball spins in and strikes Khawaja on the pads. The fielding side are up in arms, roaring their appeals and the umpire concurs with a raised finger. Surprisingly, replays show that the ball was missing leg, making it a questionable decision.

OUT! LBW! FINCH DEPARTS! Flighted arm ball outside off, Finch goes for another sweep but this time his luck has run out and is struck on the pads. The fielding side appeals umpire raises his finger. Finch says that he has hit it and Australia quickly go in for a review. The replays show that there was no edge but the ball tracking shows that the ball just about grazed the leg stump. The verdict is umpire's call and Finch has to walk off.
Appeal for an lbw! It's given out and Finch reviews it.
13th ODI fifty for Aaron Finch.

SIX! Finch sprints to 50 off only 18 balls! That was a gigantic sweep! Tossed up down the leg side, Finch goes for a gigantic sweep sweep. The ball flies over mid-wicket and only comes back down across the fence. This is now the joint quickest ODI fifty for Australia in ODIs.
Finch on 49!

SIX! Finch is batting like a train on fire. A flatter full ball around leg, Finch hops back to make some room and powers it over long off for a maximum.
Goes on the back foot and slaps it to mid off. They cross for a brisk run and in case of a direct hit at the bowler's end, Warner would have been a run out.
A slider around middle, Warner goes deep inside the crease, nearly gets cramped up but then does well to punch it towards covers.
FOUR! Shot! Tossed up ball on off, Warner goes down and plays a neat reverse sweep through backward point for a boundary.

FOUR! Landed on the pads, Finch sweeps it with ease through backward square leg and that one finds the boundary as well.
FOUR! 50 for Australia! This is truly lightening batting we are seeing. Finch charges down the track this time and smashes it through mid-wicket for a boundary.

Australia are making this looks embarrassingly easy. Length delivery and Warner comes down again to play it through mid-wicket for a couple.
FOUR! LOFTED! Warner comes down the track and slogs it through the covers and finds the boundary.

DOT BALL! Wow, that's a rarity. Shortish and on off, slapped on the off side but straight to covers. 18 runs off the over!
Slower again, full and on middle, it's flicked through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.

SIX! Boom! Finch is targeting Perera here and he has scooted to 33 off 10 balls in no time. His partner is yet to get off the mark. A slower full ball on off, Finch picks it early and launches it over long on for a biggie. The crowd has gone silent.
FOUR! Finch is on fire and Australia are off to a flier! On a length and angling into the batsman, Finch attacks it with all his might and dismisses it over mid on for a boundary.

FOUR! Lucky boundary! An over-pitched ball outside off, Finch winds up for a big shot, he was targeting the long on fence probably but it flies off the leading edge and goes over backward point for a boundary.
Fuller length delivery sliding down the leg side, Finch clips it through square leg and returns for the second run.
Finch has punched the ball off the backfoot. They pick up a single.
Fullish ball on the stumps, Finch sweeps it fine down the leg side.

FOUR! 4 IN 4! That was a delicious shot! Fuller ball outside off, Finch comes forward and lofts it. The beauty nearly goes all the way for a maximum but bounces just before the boundary at extra cover. The umpire raises both hands but changes his decision to a boundary after a while.
FOUR! PUNCHED! Finch is getting comfortable here. Third boundary in a row! Aponso bowls it short and Finch punches is off the back foot and the ball races to the boundary at point.

FOUR! DROPPED! Riskily done by Finch! Full on off, Finch plays a lofted drive but can't quite make solid contact with the ball. It is hit hard though and Thisara Perera at mid on leaps high to catch it. The ball bounces out of his hand and goes all the way to the fence.

FOUR! Tossed up outside off and spinning in, Finch looks to sweep it but misses and the ball hits his pads. There is an appeal for LBW but his leg was outside off. The ball goes past the slips to the boundary at third man.
Amila Aponso to bowl from the other end.

Welcome back. Thankfully, the rain has stopped and there isn't much of a delay in beginning the chase. Aaron Finch and David Warner are the Aussie openers. It will be Thisara Perera to kickoff proceedings. Here we go...
